tests.weakness: User input is concatenated into SMTP MAIL FROM/RCPT TO and IMAP SELECT commands; CRLF injection adds an extra recipient (delivered by Mailpit) and an extra IMAP CREATE command (executed by Dovecot).

Native C service compiled -fno-stack-protector -z execstack -no-pie: strcpy overflows a 64-byte buffer into an adjacent canary (and crashes on long input); printf(user_input) leaks stack pointers (%p), reads arbitrary strings (%s) and writes memory (%n).

A filename is stored benignly (HTML-escaped, no execution) by the portal, then later concatenated into a shell command by a separate export worker, detonating the incubated payload (id output + in-range callback).
A legacy raw-socket service writes the decoded lang parameter verbatim into Set-Cookie without stripping CR/LF, so %0d%0a injects an extra header or a whole second response.

tests.surface: POST :8616 (CL-framing proxy) with obfuscated Transfer-Encoding + innocent GET on same connection
tests.weakness: The front proxy frames by Content-Length only while the backend honours obfuscated Transfer-Encoding (xchunked) as chunked; the CL.TE desync lets a smuggled prefix poison the next request, which receives the smuggled response.

Absolute reset links are built from Host/X-Forwarded-Host (attacker host reflected), duplicate Host headers are accepted, and a cache keyed on URL only serves a Host-poisoned response to later visitors.

URL fetcher has no allowlist: reaches an internal-only unpublished service, a cloud-metadata-style endpoint on 169.254.169.254 (fake IAM creds), reads local files via file:// and speaks gopher:// to internal hosts.
The model binder binds every supplied JSON field, so a normal user escalates by adding is_admin/role/balance the UI never sends, then reads the admin-only flag.

The CSV export writes user-controlled cells unescaped, so =cmd|... (DDE) and =HYPERLINK(...) prefixes survive as formulas; opening the export interprets them and the HYPERLINK exfiltrates to an in-range listener.
tests.degraded: Spreadsheet client is simulated by the in-range csv-open service (no headless Excel available); the unescaped formula export and HYPERLINK exfil to an in-range listener are faithful, DDE commands are recorded rather than executed.

tests.weakness: Python pickle.loads() and PHP unserialize() (no allowed_classes) accept attacker payloads: a pickle __reduce__ chain executes code (reads flag/id) and a PHP Report->Reader __toString POP chain reads the flag while Executor __destruct runs shell commands.

The SERVER validates redirect targets (substring/relative-path checks) and fetches them server-side, but //evil, %2f%2fevil, \/\/evil and https://trusted.lab@evil bypass validation, yielding a 302 to an attacker host with the server-side fetch logged.

The PDF/document renderer loads user-controlled HTML with web security disabled and file access allowed, so injected JS reads file:///etc/passwd, performs SSRF to the internal-only service and executes inside the rendering context.

Username validation uses the catastrophically-backtracking regex ^(a+)+$ with no input length or time limit; a short input returns in milliseconds while a crafted ~28-char input takes seconds (superlinear).
